hints: Friction acts only while the velocities differ: it slows the block and drives the plank. Draw both on one v–t graph.
worded:
1. (i) Kinetic friction μmg = 0.1mg: the block decelerates at 1 m/s²; the plank (4m) accelerates at 0.1mg/4m = 0.25 m/s².

2. (ii) Equal velocities: 4 − t = 0.25t, so t = 3.2 s, common velocity 0.8 m/s.

3. (iii) After that they move together on a smooth floor with no external horizontal force: friction is zero.

4. (iv) Block: 4 × 3.2 − ½ × 3.2² = 7.68 m. Plank: ½ × 0.25 × 3.2² = 1.28 m.

5. (v) The block slides 7.68 − 1.28 = 6.4 m along the plank, so the plank must be at least 6.4 m long.

6. Check by momentum: 4m = 5m × v gives v = 0.8 m/s, as above.

**Another way: plank frame.** Relative to the plank the block starts at 4 m/s and decelerates at 1 + 0.25 = 1.25 m/s²: it stops relative to the plank after 4/1.25 = 3.2 s, having slid 4²/(2 × 1.25) = 6.4 m.
mistakes: Once the velocities are equal, friction is zero (no force tries to make them slip).

check.solved_answer: (i) 1 m/s² (retarding) and 0.25 m/s²; (ii) 3.2 s; (iii) zero; (iv) 7.68 m and 1.28 m; (v) 6.4 m.
